rows.title: blonde hedgehog
rows.summary: The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus), also known as the West European hedgehog, Western European hedgehog or common hedgehog, is a hedgehog species native to Europe from Iberia and Italy northwards into Scandinavia and westwards into Ireland. They are extremely rare, except on North Ronaldsay and the Channel Island of Alderney, where around 25% of the population is thought to be blonde.

rows.title: Jersey orchid
rows.summary: A. laxiflora is common in Normandy and Brittany (France), but in the United Kingdom it is represented only on the Channel Islands, where in Jersey it is called Jersey orchid and in Guernsey it is called Loose Flowered orchid .

rows.title: western green lizard
rows.evidence: The source names 'western green lizard' and 'Jersey'.
rows.summary: All are protected species, with Jersey being the only native habitat in the British Isles for the green lizard, wall lizard, spiny toad and agile frog.

rows.title: Guernsey vole
rows.summary: The Guernsey vole (Microtus arvalis sarnius), known in Guernésiais as the mulot, is a subspecies of the common vole endemic to the island of Guernsey in the Channel Islands.

rows.title: red-billed chough
rows.evidence: The source names 'red-billed chough' and 'Isle of Man'.
rows.summary: The red-billed chough, Cornish chough or simply chough ( CHUF; Pyrrhocorax pyrrhocorax) is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax. P. p. pyrrhocorax, the nominate subspecies and smallest form, is endemic to the British Isles, where it is restricted to Ireland, the Isle of Man, and the west of Wales, southwest Scotland, and Cornwall, which it recolonised in 2001 after an absence of 50 years.

rows.title: St Kilda dandelion
rows.evidence: The source names 'St Kilda dandelion' and 'St Kilda'.
rows.summary: Taraxacum pankhurstianum, also known as the St Kilda dandelion, is a species of dandelion that was identified as new in 2012 after being cultivated at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh from seeds collected two years previously on the island of Hirta, the largest island in the St Kilda archipelago, on the western edge of Scotland.

rows.title: St Kilda wren
rows.evidence: The source names 'St Kilda wren' and 'St Kilda'.
rows.summary: The St Kilda wren (Troglodytes troglodytes hirtensis) is a small passerine bird in the wren family. It is a distinctive subspecies of the Eurasian wren, endemic to the islands of the isolated St Kilda archipelago, in the Atlantic Ocean 64 kilometres (40 mi) west of the Outer Hebrides, Scotland.

rows.title: St Kilda field mouse
rows.evidence: The source names 'St Kilda field mouse' and 'St Kilda'.
rows.summary: The St Kilda field mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus hirtensis) is a subspecies of the wood mouse that is endemic to the Scottish archipelago of St Kilda, the island 64 kilometres (40 mi) west of Benbecula in the Outer Hebrides, and 160 kilometres (100 mi) from mainland Scotland.

rows.title: Fair Isle wren
rows.evidence: The source names 'Fair Isle wren' and 'Fair Isle'.
rows.summary: The Fair Isle wren (Troglodytes troglodytes fridariensis) is a small passerine bird in the wren family. It is a subspecies of the Eurasian wren endemic to Fair Isle, Shetland, Scotland, an island about halfway between mainland Shetland and Orkney.

rows.title: Shetland wren
rows.summary: The Shetland wren (Troglodytes troglodytes zetlandicus) is a small passerine bird in the wren family. It is a subspecies of the Eurasian wren, endemic to the Shetland archipelago of Scotland, with the exception of Fair Isle which has its own endemic subspecies, the Fair Isle wren.

rows.title: Salvelinus gracillimus
rows.summary: Salvelinus gracillimus is a cold-water species of fish in the family Salmonidae. The species is endemic to Loch of Girlsta in the Shetland Islands; reports of specimens from Loch More on the Scottish mainland are unconfirmed.

rows.title: Orkney vole
rows.summary: The Orkney vole (Microtus arvalis orcadensis) is a population of the common vole found in the Orkney Islands, off the northern coast of Scotland.

rows.title: Skomer vole
rows.summary: The Skomer vole (Clethrionomys glareolus skomerensis) is a subspecies of bank vole endemic to the island of Skomer, off the west coast of Wales.

rows.title: Islay shrew
rows.summary: Sorex araneus grantii is a subspecies of the shrew Sorex araneus, found only on the Scottish island of Islay.

rows.title: Lundy cabbage
rows.summary: Coincya wrightii, known as Lundy cabbage, is a species of primitive brassicoid, endemic to the island of Lundy off the southwestern coast of England, where it is sufficiently isolated to have formed its own species, with its endemic phytophagous beetles.

rows.title: Lundy cabbage flea beetle
rows.evidence: The source names 'Lundy cabbage flea beetle' and 'Lundy'.
rows.summary: Psylliodes luridipennis, commonly known as the Lundy cabbage flea beetle or the bronze Lundy cabbage flea beetle, is a species of flea beetle endemic to the island of Lundy, where it lives and feeds upon the endemic Lundy cabbage (Coincya wrightii).

rows.title: Orkney charr
rows.summary: Salvelinus inframundus, also known as Orkney charr, is an extinct cold-water fish in the family Salmonidae which was endemic to Hoy Island, Orkney, Scotland.

rows.title: Arran service-tree
rows.summary: Hedlundia pseudofennica, also called Arran service-tree or Arran cut-leaved whitebeam, is a species of plant in the family Rosaceae. Endemic to the Isle of Arran in Scotland, it is threatened by habitat loss.

rows.title: Arran whitebeam
rows.summary: Hedlundia arranensis, sometimes referred to as the Scottish or Arran whitebeam, is a species of plant in the family Rosaceae. It is endemic to the island of Arran in Scotland.

rows.title: Catacol whitebeam
rows.summary: Hedlundia pseudomeinichii, known as false rowan and Catacol whitebeam, is a rare species of tree endemic to the Isle of Arran in south-western Scotland.

rows.title: Atlantic puffin
rows.evidence: The source names 'Atlantic puffin' and 'Puffin Island'.
rows.summary: Puffin Island (Irish: Oileán na gCánóg), historically called Inishfearglin, is an uninhabited steep rocky island lying off the coast of the Iveragh Peninsula, County Kerry, Ireland. Puffin Island holds important populations of several seabird species, including Atlantic puffins, Manx shearwaters and European storm-petrels, and was acquired as a nature reserve by the Irish Wildbird Conservancy (now BirdWatch Ireland) in the early 1980s.

rows.title: roseate tern
rows.summary: The roseate tern (Sterna dougallii) is a species of tern in the family Laridae. The largest European colony, accounting for more than 75% of the European population, is in Ireland, at Rockabill Island, County Dublin.

rows.title: Shetland mouse-ear
rows.summary: Cerastium nigrescens var. nigrescens, commonly known as the Shetland mouse-ear, Shetland mouse-eared chickweed or Edmondston's chickweed, is an endemic variety of Arctic Chickweed, Cerastium nigrescens, found in Shetland, Scotland. Although reported from two other sites in the 19th century, it currently grows only on two serpentine hills on the island of Unst.

rows.title: European dark bee
rows.evidence: The source names 'European dark bee' and 'Colonsay'.
rows.summary: Colonsay and Oronsay are home to about 50 colonies of the European dark bee, Apis mellifera mellifera.

rows.title: razorbill
rows.summary: The breeding colonies of razorbills and guillemots on Handa are the largest in the UK, representing 11% and 9% of the total British population respectively.

rows.title: Least adder's-tongue
rows.evidence: The source names "Least adder's-tongue" and 'St Agnes'.
rows.summary: Ophioglossum lusitanicum, the least adder's-tongue, is a small fern of the family Ophioglossaceae. The distribution in Britain is restricted to one small area of coastal heath on St Agnes, Isles of Scilly where it was discovered by John Raven in 1950.

rows.title: Wild peony
rows.evidence: The source names 'Wild peony' and 'Steep Holm'.
rows.summary: Steep Holm and Flat Holm are the only known places in the UK where the wild peony has naturalised.

rows.title: Wild leek
rows.evidence: The source names 'Wild leek' and 'Flat Holm'.
rows.summary: It forms part of the City and County of Cardiff and is now managed by Cardiff Council's Flat Holm Project Team and designated as a Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest and a Special Protection Area, because of the maritime grassland and rare plants such as rock sea-lavender (Limonium binervosum) and wild leek (Allium ampeloprasum).

rows.title: Red squirrel
rows.evidence: The source names 'Red squirrel' and 'Brownsea Island'.
rows.summary: The red squirrel (Sciurus vulgaris), also called Eurasian red squirrel, is a species of tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus. Brownsea Island in Poole Harbour is also populated exclusively by red rather than grey squirrels .

rows.title: European storm petrel
rows.evidence: The source names 'European storm petrel' and 'Annet'.
rows.summary: What Annet is famous for is its colonies of Manx shearwaters and storm petrels; but since they nest underground, and only come and go in the dark, there is nothing to be seen of them by day.
